title: Can LLMs generate Enterprise Quality Code? — Prasenjit Sarkar, Sonar
talk_summary: Sonar ran 4,444 open-source Java assignments through 53+ models and measured not just functional pass rate but issue density, cyclomatic/cognitive complexity, verbosity (LOC), and security issues per million LOC, publishing a leaderboard. They then describe an agent-centric loop: pre-commit static analysis via MCP inside the coding agent (1-5s vs 1-5min CI), PR-level analysis, and a remediation agent that fixes issues but re-runs analysis and compilation and discards fixes that regress.

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate each model on a fixed task corpus and score issue density, complexity, LOC verbosity, and security issues per million LOC, not just functional correctness.
takeaways.numbers: 4,444 Java assignments; 53+ models; Gemini 3.1 Pro High 84.17% pass, 307k LOC, 614 bugs/M LOC, 210 security issues/M LOC; Claude Sonnet 4.6 ~300 security issues/M LOC, 627k LOC; GPT 5.4 ~1.2M LOC; GPT 5.2 High ~1M LOC vs GPT 4.0 <250k LOC

takeaways.technique: Pre-commit static analysis inside the agent loop via MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a static analyzer as an MCP tool the coding agent calls before committing; it returns issues in seconds and the agent fixes them before a PR exists.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before you commit that, before you push that into PR, you just need to analyze my code... this analysis is going to take about 1 to 5 seconds

takeaways.technique: Fix-then-reverify remediation loop with discard on regression
takeaways.what_they_do: Remediation agent generates a fix, re-runs analysis and compilation, and throws the fix away if it introduces new issues, one PR per issue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the remediation agent is going to create the fix, run it through the analysis again, run it through the compilation part again... If there is an issues, it is going to discard it

takeaways.technique: Verbosity as a routing cost signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Track LOC generated per task per model; newer models are far more verbose, which raises review and compute cost even at equal pass rates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the newer models that we are seeing coming up... the kind of lines of code is going to the north
takeaways.numbers: GPT 5.2 High ~1M LOC vs GPT 4.0 <250k LOC for same 4,400 assignments (~4x)

takeaways.technique: Expect finer-grained defects from stronger models
takeaways.what_they_do: Observe that as models mature, total vulnerabilities fall but remaining bugs get subtler and harder for humans to spot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're also creating some more finer bugs that is very very hard for a human being to detect

takeaways.what_they_do: Push relevant codebase and architecture context into the model because base models don't know company code or architecture.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it does have the limited context which is obviously doesn't understand the company's data or company's code base or company's architecture
